input.quote: 19.4 For breach of Section 19.1 or 19.2, Vendor shall promptly re-perform, repair, or replace the nonconforming item at no charge. If Vendor cannot do so within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of Fees paid for it.
input.rationale: Section 19 satisfies the fallback and most of the preferred checklist. 19.1 warrants that Services are performed in a professional and workmanlike manner and that Services and Deliverables materially conform to their documentation and specifications; 19.2 gives each Deliverable ninety days after delivery or acceptance and, because "Services" is defined (1.7) to include the hosted software, warrants hosted-software conformity "throughout the subscription term" — far longer than the 90-day software / 30-day services floors. 19.4 supplies repair/re-performance/replacement with a refund of Fees paid, and is non-exclusive for key claims; 19.3 adds malicious-code and Applicable Law warranties, and 19.5's disclaimer is mutual and expressly does not limit the express warranties or remedies. Two points short of full preferred wording are noted only: the Deliverable conformity period is ninety days rather than twelve months (the hosted software itself runs for the whole term), and the malicious-code warranty is qualified to code "intentionally introduced by Vendor." Neither is material enough to redline, so we accept the clause as sitting at or above the fallback.
